title: How do we adapt to the cold?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: more than anything else; used to emphasise the most important feature of something
able to endure difficult conditions without being damaged
be familiar with; be accustomed to
(idiom) partly and partly not; used when there is no clear answer to a question
based on someone's personal experience rather than objective facts
shaking movement your muscles make because of feeling cold or frightened

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，这里是 BBC Learning English 的 6 Minute English。

sentences.en: I'm Phil. And I'm Becca. 6-Minute-English listeners are truly global, coming from all over the world, including some of the coldest countries on Earth – places like Finland, where winter temperatures drop to -20°C.
sentences.zh: 我是 Phil。我是 Becca。6-Minute-English 的听众遍布全球，他们来自世界各地，包括地球上一些最寒冷的国家——比如芬兰，那里的冬季气温会降到零下20摄氏度。

sentences.en: Are you good at dealing with the cold, Phil?
sentences.zh: Phil，你擅长御寒吗？

sentences.en: I'm not sure, but I do know that I don't like it.
sentences.zh: 我不太确定，但我确实知道我不喜欢冷。

sentences.en: What about you, Becca? Well, I'd rather be too hot and cool down than too cold and try to warm up.
sentences.zh: 你呢，Becca？好吧，我宁愿热得不行再降温，也不愿冻得要死再想办法暖和起来。

sentences.en: Yes, me too. Here in the UK, it never gets as cold as Finland, but it's not unusual to see some people dressed in T-shirts while others are wrapped up in warm clothes.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也是。在英国，天气从不像芬兰那么冷，但看到有些人穿着 T 恤，而另一些人却裹着厚衣服，这并不罕见。

sentences.en: Why do people feel the cold so differently?
sentences.zh: 为什么人们对寒冷的感觉如此不同？

sentences.en: That's what we'll be discussing in this episode, as well as learning some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们本期节目要讨论的内容，同时我们还会学习一些实用的新单词和短语。

sentences.en: And as always, you'll find all the vocabulary from this episode, plus a quiz and worksheet, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到本期节目的所有词汇，以及测验和工作单。

sentences.en: But now I have a question for you, Becca.
sentences.zh: 不过现在我有一个问题要问你，Becca。

sentences.en: According to the Guinness Book of World Records, the lowest temperature ever recorded was a very cold -89°C... but where?
sentences.zh: 根据吉尼斯世界纪录，有记录以来的最低气温是极寒的零下89摄氏度……但这是在哪里呢？

sentences.en: Was it: a) the Arctic, b) Antarctica, or c) the top of Mount Everest?
sentences.zh: 是：a) 北极，b) 南极，还是 c) 珠穆朗玛峰顶？

sentences.en: Hmm. I'm going to guess b) Antarctica. OK.
sentences.zh: 嗯。我猜是 b) 南极。好的。

sentences.en: Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们将在节目最后揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Our experience of cold depends on many things, including our genes, culture and place of birth, but perhaps the most obvious thing is the clothes we wear.
sentences.zh: 我们对寒冷的体验取决于很多因素，包括我们的基因、文化和出生地，但也许最显而易见的是我们穿的衣服。

sentences.en: Professor Gunhild Sætren lives on the icy island of Svalbard, 800 miles inside the Arctic Circle.
sentences.zh: Gunhild Sætren 教授住在冰天雪地的斯瓦尔巴群岛，这里位于北极圈内800英里处。

sentences.en: Here, she advises presenter Caroline Steel on how to dress against the cold, for BBC World Service programme CrowdScience.
sentences.zh: 在这里，她为 BBC World Service 节目 CrowdScience 的主持人 Caroline Steel 提供关于如何穿衣防寒的建议。

sentences.en: So, what should we consider when choosing our clothes?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们在选择衣服时应该考虑什么呢？

sentences.en: Gunhild Sætren First and foremost, I would say that perhaps the gender differs.
sentences.zh: Gunhild Sætren：首先，我想说，也许性别存在差异。

sentences.en: So, males often are more tolerant, perhaps, than females.
sentences.zh: 所以，男性可能往往比女性更耐寒。

sentences.en: Then it's of course what you're used to.
sentences.zh: 然后当然就是你习惯了什么。

sentences.en: Are you used to dealing with the cold? Are you not?
sentences.zh: 你习惯应对寒冷吗？还是不习惯？

sentences.en: Gunhild says that first and foremost, men and women feel the cold differently.
sentences.zh: Gunhild 说，首先，男性和女性对寒冷的感觉不同。

sentences.en: She uses the phrase first and foremost to mean 'more than anything else'.
sentences.zh: 她用 first and foremost 这个短语来表示“最重要的事情”。

sentences.en: She wants to emphasise that something – in this case, someone's gender – is the most important thing to consider.
sentences.zh: 她想强调某件事——在这个例子中是人的性别——是需要考虑的最重要的事情。

sentences.en: There is some debate about whether men or women are more tolerant of the cold.
sentences.zh: 关于男性还是女性更耐寒，存在一些争议。

sentences.en: Being tolerant of something means being able to endure it without getting hurt.
sentences.zh: 对某事 tolerant（耐受）意味着能够忍受它而不受伤害。

sentences.en: Another important factor is whether you are used to the cold – if being in cold environments is something you're familiar with.
sentences.zh: 另一个重要因素是你是否习惯了寒冷——即置身于寒冷的环境中是否是你所熟悉的事情。

sentences.en: It might sound obvious that someone born in Arctic Svalbard would feel less cold than someone born in Brazil, but apart from environmental factors, are there actual physical differences that allow people to cope better with the cold?
sentences.zh: 听起来显而易见，出生在北极斯瓦尔巴群岛的人会比出生在巴西的人感觉不那么冷，但除了环境因素外，是否真的存在身体上的差异，让人们能够更好地应对寒冷？

sentences.en: Dr Cara Ocobock studies reindeer herders in northern Finland – people who live in cold temperatures every day and have done for centuries.
sentences.zh: Cara Ocobock 博士研究了芬兰北部的驯鹿牧民——这些人每天都生活在寒冷的气温中，且已经持续了几个世纪。

sentences.en: She measures their reaction to extreme cold and compares it to ordinary Finns from warmer parts of the country.
sentences.zh: 她测量了他们对极端寒冷的反应，并将其与来自该国较温暖地区的普通芬兰人进行对比。

sentences.en: Here, Cara shares her findings with Caroline Steel from BBC World Service's CrowdScience.
sentences.zh: 在这里，Cara 与 BBC World Service 节目 CrowdScience 的 Caroline Steel 分享了她的发现。

sentences.en: OK. My guess is the reindeer herders deal better in the cold.
sentences.zh: 好的。我猜驯鹿牧民在寒冷中应对得更好。

sentences.en: Yes and no. The more data we collect within this area, the more confusing the picture gets.
sentences.zh: 介于两者之间（可以说对，也可以说不对）。我们在这一领域收集的数据越多，情况就越让人困惑。

sentences.en: I can say that subjectively, at this point, the reindeer herders, at least kind of mentally, handle the cold far better.
sentences.zh: 我可以说，从主观上来看，在目前这个阶段，驯鹿牧民至少在心理上能更好地应对寒冷。

sentences.en: They are far less likely to shiver. So, do the reindeer herders deal better with the cold?
sentences.zh: 他们发抖的可能性要小得多。那么，驯鹿牧民能更好地应对寒冷吗？

sentences.en: The answer is yes and no – a phrase meaning partly and partly not, used when there's no clear answer to a question.
sentences.zh: 答案是 yes and no——这个短语的意思是“部分是，部分不是”，用于对一个问题没有明确答案的时候。

sentences.en: However, Cara does say subjectively, the herders manage better.
sentences.zh: 不过，Cara 确实说过，从主观上来看，牧民们应对得更好。

sentences.en: They don't feel so cold. Subjectively means based on your personal inner experience rather than objective facts.
sentences.zh: 他们不觉得那么冷。Subjectively（主观地）意味着基于你个人的内心体验，而不是客观事实。

sentences.en: And physically there are differences too.
sentences.zh: 而且在身体上也有差异。

sentences.en: Reindeer herders are less likely to shiver – the shaky movement that cold muscles make to try and warm them up.
sentences.zh: 驯鹿牧民不太容易发抖（shiver）——即寒冷的肌肉为了试图让自己暖和起来而做出的颤抖动作。

sentences.en: In fact, how we experience the cold is probably a combination of everything we've discussed, including genetic adaptations passed on from parents to children.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们对寒冷的体验可能是我们讨论过的所有因素的结合，包括从父母传给孩子的基因适应性。

sentences.en: Right, I'm off to find my gloves and woolly hat, so why don't you reveal the answer to the question, Phil?
sentences.zh: 好了，我要去找我的手套和羊毛帽了，那么 Phil，你何不揭晓那个问题的答案呢？

sentences.en: Yes, I asked where the lowest temperature on Earth was ever recorded.
sentences.zh: 好的，我之前问过地球上有记录以来的最低气温是在哪里。

sentences.en: You said b) Antarctica. And that is... the right answer.
sentences.zh: 你说是 b) 南极。而那……就是正确答案。

sentences.en: The lowest temperature ever recorded on Earth was at the Vostok Research Station in Antarctica in 1983.
sentences.zh: 地球上有记录以来的最低气温是1983年在南极洲的东方站（Vostok Research Station）录得的。

sentences.en: Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with the phrase first and foremost, meaning more than anything else.
sentences.zh: 让我们复习一下学过的词汇，首先是短语 first and foremost，意思是“最重要的事情”。

sentences.en: A person who is tolerant of something is able to endure it without being hurt.
sentences.zh: 一个对某事 tolerant（耐受）的人能够忍受它而不受伤害。

sentences.en: If you're used to something, you're familiar with it.
sentences.zh: 如果你对某事 used to（习惯于），说明你对它很熟悉。

sentences.en: The idiom yes and no means partly and partly not, and is used when you can't give a clear answer to a question.
sentences.zh: 习语 yes and no 意思是“部分是，部分不是”，用于当你无法对一个问题给出明确答案时。

sentences.en: The adverb subjectively means in a way that's based on your personal experience rather than objective facts.
sentences.zh: 副词 subjectively（主观地）意味着以一种基于你个人经验而非客观事实的方式。

sentences.en: And finally, a shiver is the shaking movement made by your muscles when you feel cold or afraid.
sentences.zh: 最后，shiver（发抖）是指当你感到寒冷或害怕时，肌肉做出的颤抖动作。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but remember you'll find a quiz and a worksheet for this episode on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟时间又到了，但请记住，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到本期节目的测验和工作单。

sentences.en: See you there soon, but for now, it's goodbye.
sentences.zh: 期待与你在那里相见，不过现在，要说再见啦。

sentences.en: Bye!
sentences.zh: 再见！
